entities.summary:
Francesco Crasso (1500–1566) was an Italian Roman Catholic cardinal. As a diplomat and politician, he played a crucial role in the Holy Roman Empire's diplomatic relations with European powers during the Renaissance. Francesco Crasso was instrumental in negotiating the Treaty of Augsburg (1555), which ended the Thirty Years' War and established the Peace of Augsburg. This treaty marked a significant shift in the balance of power in Europe, as it recognized Protestantism as a legitimate religion within the Holy Roman Empire. 

Crasso's legacy extends beyond his diplomatic achievements. He was a patron of the arts and architecture, commissioning several notable projects, including the construction of the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Milan. Francesco Crasso died on September 7, 1566, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential cardinals of his time. 

The impact of Francesco Crasso's life and work can still be felt today. His diplomatic efforts helped shape the modern nation-state system, while his patronage of the arts continues to inspire artists and architects around the world.
